hypothesis: Role-bound episode signatures provide retrieval quality or complete retained-state/latency advantage over exact structural indexing with the same supplied annotations.
scope: Synthetic structured admission experiment; no learned extraction, natural-language entailment or production engine integration claim.
encoding: Production PhaseHVec role-qualified atoms, binding and bundling; seven nonempty role projections per episode; pack binary phases into existing research BitVec/popcount scorer. One fixed configuration; no evaluation tuning.
validation: packed scorer parity with native phase similarity

promotion.safety: zero unsupported, wrong-source, wrong-version, wrong-namespace, invalid-time or deleted outputs
promotion.quality: recall at least 0.99 and no more than 0.01 below exact baseline in every case
promotion.advantage: At matched quality, at least 20 percent lower end-to-end median query latency OR total retained allocation including canonical records and codebook; no more than 10 percent query/ingest/update/reopen regression in any case for the selected arm
promotion.consistency: one unchanged arm must satisfy the gates across all seeds, corpus sizes and interference levels
promotion.stop: No production promotion if no arm passes. No post-evaluation parameter tuning or more expensive learned evaluation to rescue a failure.

limits: All canonical facts supplied equally to every method; this is an oracle-extraction control.
BM25 is the existing research implementation over shared roleless token IDs, not a measurement of native HMS hybrid search.
Exact role postings plus source verification is the decisive baseline; existing failed surface-order contrast results are retained, not rerun.
Allocation accounting is not RSS; process peak RSS will be reported separately.
Only local/free resources; no API calls, cloud work, model downloads or production changes.
